title: How CounterCrave Evaluates Kitchen Appliances
description: See the research, comparison and testing standards CounterCrave uses for kitchen appliance recommendations.
summary: CounterCrave evaluates products against task-specific criteria instead of relying on popularity alone. Every recommendation should explain its evidence, trade-offs, ideal user and meaningful limitations.

sections.heading: Our evidence hierarchy
paragraphs: We begin with current manufacturer documentation, manuals, safety notices and verified specifications. We then compare competing models on criteria that matter to the page's search intent.
When a product has been tested directly, the article explains the test conditions. When direct testing has not occurred, the page must not imply otherwise.
bullets: Hands-on measurements and observations when available
Cross-checked specifications and current model details
Original comparison tables and decision criteria
Clearly attributed expert or authoritative sources

sections.heading: What we measure
paragraphs: Criteria vary by product category. Common factors include usable capacity, performance for the intended task, consistency, controls, cleaning effort, noise, countertop footprint, materials, warranty and value.
A high score in one category does not automatically make a product the best choice for every reader.

sections.heading: How recommendations are written
paragraphs: Recommendation pages include a quick verdict, comparison context, who should buy, who should skip, important drawbacks and alternatives.
Prices and availability can change. CounterCrave normally uses a 'Check price on Amazon' link instead of hardcoding a price that may become inaccurate.

sections.heading: Corrections and updates
paragraphs: Meaningful content changes receive an updated date. A date is not changed simply to make an old article appear fresh.
Readers can report an error through the contact page. Material errors should be corrected promptly and transparently.

author: CounterCrave Editorial Team
